passages.title: 壽山的香蕉小偷
passages.text: Last Sunday, my family went hiking on Shoushan in Kaohsiung. There are many wild monkeys on the mountain. Before we started, a park worker said, "Don't {1} the monkeys, and don't show them any food." But my little brother didn't listen. He took a {2} out of his bag because he was hungry. In one second, a big monkey jumped down from a tree and took it from his hand! The monkey sat on a rock, ate the banana, and threw the peel at us. My brother started to {3}. Then two more monkeys came and opened Mom's bag. They took all our {4} and an apple. Mom shouted, "Hey! That's our lunch!" After that, we put all our {5} deep in our bags and walked fast. Now my brother says monkeys are the best thieves in Taiwan.

blanks.why: Don't feed the monkeys.「不要餵猴子。」，後面也說不要讓牠們看到食物。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）接 the monkeys 都不通。
弟弟餓了，從包包拿出一根香蕉 banana，後面猴子把它吃掉、丟果皮。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）都不能吃、也沒有果皮。
香蕉被搶走，弟弟哭 cry 了起來。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、borrow（借）都不是被搶東西後的反應。
猴子拿走了我們的葡萄 grapes 和一顆蘋果，媽媽說那是午餐。tickets（票）、pockets（口袋）、offices（辦公室）都不能當午餐。
把水果 fruit 藏在包包深處，以免又被猴子搶。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不會吸引猴子、也不能裝進包包。

passages.zh: 上週日，我們全家去高雄壽山爬山。山上有很多野生猴子。出發前，一位園區人員說：「不要餵猴子，也不要讓牠們看到任何食物。」可是弟弟沒聽進去，他肚子餓，從包包裡拿出一根香蕉。一秒鐘內，一隻大猴子從樹上跳下來，從他手上把香蕉搶走！猴子坐在石頭上吃完香蕉，還把皮丟向我們。弟弟哭了出來。接著又來了兩隻猴子，打開媽媽的包包，把我們的葡萄和一顆蘋果全拿走了。媽媽大喊：「喂！那是我們的午餐！」從那之後，我們把所有水果都塞進包包深處，快步往前走。現在弟弟說，猴子是台灣最厲害的小偷。

passages.title: 妹妹的檸檬汁小攤
passages.text: Last summer, my little sister Mia wanted to buy a new bike. She didn't have enough money, so she decided to sell lemonade in front of our house. She bought ten {1} at the market and some sugar. Mom helped her make the drink, and I made a sign for her. On the first day, it was very hot, and many people walking by were {2}. Mia sold thirty cups! But on the second day, it rained, and nobody came. Then Mia had an idea. She cut up some {3}, like {4} and strawberries, and put it into the lemonade. She called it "Rainy Day Rainbow Drink." People laughed and bought it. After three weeks, she had {5} money for the bike. Now she rides it to school every day and tells everyone, "This bike is made of lemons!"

blanks.why: 買了十顆檸檬 lemons 和糖來做檸檬汁。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、pockets（口袋）都不能用來做飲料。
天氣很熱，路人都口渴 thirsty，所以賣了三十杯。wooden（木製的）、national（國家的）、illegal（違法的）都不能說明大家為什麼想買飲料。
cut up some fruit「切一些水果」，放進檸檬汁裡。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能切、也不能放進飲料。
like grapes and strawberries「像是葡萄和草莓」，舉例說明切了哪些水果。letters（信）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不是水果。
have enough money「有足夠的錢」買腳踏車。ago、else、ever 都不能放在 money 前面修飾它。

passages.zh: 去年夏天，我妹妹 Mia 想買一台新腳踏車。她的錢不夠，所以決定在家門口賣檸檬汁。她在市場買了十顆檸檬和一些糖，媽媽幫她做飲料，我幫她做了一個招牌。第一天天氣很熱，很多路過的人都口渴了，Mia 賣了三十杯！但第二天下雨，一個人都沒來。後來 Mia 想到一個點子：她切了一些水果，像是葡萄和草莓，放進檸檬汁裡，取名叫「雨天彩虹飲」。大家都笑了，也買了。三個星期後，她存夠了買腳踏車的錢。現在她每天騎車上學，還跟大家說：「這台腳踏車是檸檬做的！」

passages.title: 彰化葡萄園的暑假
passages.text: This summer, I stayed at my uncle's farm in Changhua for a week. He grows {1} there. Every morning, we got up at five to pick them before the sun got too hot. My uncle showed me how to cut each bunch carefully so the {2} would not break. It was hard work, and my back hurt. But the grapes were sweet and juicy, and I could eat as many as I wanted. Besides grapes, my uncle also grows some {3} like cabbage and corn for his family. In the evening, my aunt cooked them for dinner. Everything was so {4}. On my last day, my uncle gave me a big box of grapes to take home. "You were very {5} this week," he said. "You earned it."

blanks.why: 叔叔的農場種葡萄 grapes，後面說要一串串剪下來。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、offices（辦公室）都不能種、也不能採。
小心剪下每一串，水果 fruit 才不會弄破。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不會被剪破。
vegetables like cabbage and corn「像高麗菜和玉米這樣的蔬菜」。tickets（票）、letters（信）、pockets（口袋）都不能種來煮晚餐。
剛採的菜很新鮮 fresh。honest（誠實的）、polite（有禮貌的）、lazy（懶惰的）都是形容人的，不能形容菜。
hard-working「勤奮的」，每天五點起床幫忙採收，所以叔叔說「這是你應得的」。careless（粗心的）、rude（無禮的）、lazy（懶惰的）都和「應得獎賞」矛盾。

passages.zh: 今年暑假，我在彰化叔叔的農場住了一個星期。他在那裡種葡萄。每天早上，我們五點就起床，趁太陽還沒太大之前採葡萄。叔叔教我怎麼小心地剪下每一串，才不會把果實弄破。工作很辛苦，我的背好痠，但葡萄又甜又多汁，我想吃多少就吃多少。除了葡萄，叔叔也種了一些高麗菜、玉米之類的蔬菜給家人吃。晚上嬸嬸把它們煮成晚餐，每一樣都好新鮮。最後一天，叔叔送我一大箱葡萄帶回家。「你這個星期很勤勞，」他說，「這是你應得的。」

passages.title: 不吃青菜的弟弟
passages.text: My little brother Tim hates {1}. Every time Mom puts broccoli on his plate, he hides it under his rice. One day, Mom had an idea. She took Tim to a flower market and let him {2} any seeds he wanted. He chose tomatoes and carrots. Every day after school, Tim watered his plants on the balcony. He was very {3} and never forgot. After two months, the tomatoes turned red. Tim picked one and ate it right away. "It's sweet, just like {4}!" he said. Mom smiled. "Actually, a tomato is a fruit." Then they pulled out the carrots, and Mom cooked them with beef for dinner. That night, for the first time, Tim ate all the {5} on his plate. "Food tastes better when you grow it yourself," he said.

blanks.why: hate vegetables「討厭吃青菜」，後面說他把花椰菜藏在飯底下。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、pockets（口袋）都不會被放在盤子裡。
let + 人 + choose「讓某人挑選」種子。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）接 any seeds 都不通。
very patient「很有耐心」，每天澆水從不忘記。cheap（便宜的）、wooden（木製的）、crowded（擁擠的）都不能形容人照顧植物的態度。
甜得像水果 fruit，後面媽媽說番茄其實就是水果。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都沒有甜味。
他第一次把盤子裡的蔬菜 vegetables 吃光，呼應前面他討厭青菜。letters（信）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不能吃。

passages.zh: 我弟弟 Tim 討厭吃青菜。每次媽媽把花椰菜放到他盤子上，他就把它藏到飯底下。有一天，媽媽想到一個辦法。她帶 Tim 去花市，讓他挑任何想種的種子。他選了番茄和紅蘿蔔。每天放學後，Tim 都會在陽台幫他的植物澆水，他很有耐心，從來沒忘記過。兩個月後，番茄變紅了。Tim 摘了一顆馬上吃掉。「好甜，跟水果一樣！」他說。媽媽笑著說：「其實番茄就是水果喔。」接著他們拔出紅蘿蔔，媽媽把它和牛肉一起煮成晚餐。那天晚上，Tim 第一次把盤子裡的蔬菜吃光光。「自己種的東西比較好吃。」他說。

passages.title: 狐狸與酸葡萄
passages.text: One hot afternoon, a hungry fox walked into a garden. He saw some {1} hanging high on a vine. They were purple and looked very sweet. "Those are just what I need," he said. He jumped, but he couldn't {2} them. He tried again and again, but they were too high. Finally, he was too {3} to jump anymore. He walked away and said, "Those grapes are probably as sour as a {4}. I'd rather eat a {5} anyway." A little bird in the tree laughed. "When you can't get something, it's easy to say it isn't good," she said. People still tell this story today. When someone says bad things about what they can't have, we call it "sour grapes."

blanks.why: 藤蔓上高高掛著紫色的葡萄 grapes。tickets（票）、letters（信）、offices（辦公室）都不會長在藤蔓上。
reach「搆到」：狐狸跳起來還是搆不到葡萄。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、borrow（借）都和跳起來拿東西無關。
too tired to…「累到無法…」，跳了很多次。wooden（木製的）、cheap（便宜的）、national（國家的）都不能形容身體狀態。
as sour as a lemon「像檸檬一樣酸」。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都沒有酸味可以比較。
I'd rather eat a banana「我寧可吃香蕉」。museum（博物館）、corner（角落）、letter（信）都不能吃。

passages.zh: 一個炎熱的下午，一隻飢餓的狐狸走進一座花園。牠看到藤蔓上高高掛著一些葡萄，紫色的，看起來非常甜。「這正是我需要的。」牠說。牠跳了起來，卻搆不到。牠一試再試，但葡萄實在太高了。最後，牠累得再也跳不動，便一邊走開一邊說：「那些葡萄八成跟檸檬一樣酸，反正我寧可吃香蕉。」樹上的一隻小鳥笑了：「得不到的東西，說它不好最容易了。」直到今天，人們還在說這個故事。當有人說自己得不到的東西的壞話時，我們就說那是「酸葡萄」。

passages.title: 瑪利歐賽車的香蕉皮
passages.text: In Mario Kart, one of the most famous items is the {1} peel. When you drop it on the road, other players who drive over it will spin around. My friends and I play every Friday night. Last week, I was in first place in the last lap. I was so {2}! But then my friend Jerry dropped three banana peels in front of me. I hit all of them and fell to eighth place. Everyone laughed except me. After the game, Mom brought us a plate of {3}: apples, oranges, and real bananas. Jerry picked up a {4} and said, "Be careful. Don't drop the peel." We all laughed again. I told him, "Next week, I will {5} more, and you will be the one who spins!"

blanks.why: banana peel「香蕉皮」，丟在路上會讓別人打轉。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）都沒有「皮」。
最後一圈跑第一，所以非常興奮 excited。wooden（木製的）、crowded（擁擠的）、national（國家的）都不能形容人的心情。
a plate of fruit「一盤水果」，冒號後面列出蘋果、柳丁、香蕉。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能裝在盤子裡。
拿起一根香蕉 banana，還開玩笑叫我別丟香蕉皮。pocket（口袋）、museum（博物館）、corner（角落）都沒有皮可以丟。
practice more「多練習」，下週才能贏回來。marry（結婚）、spell（拼字）、lend（借出）都不能說明怎麼變強。

passages.zh: 在《瑪利歐賽車》裡，最有名的道具之一就是香蕉皮。把它丟在路上，開過去的其他玩家就會打轉。我和朋友每週五晚上都會玩。上週，我在最後一圈跑第一，超級興奮！但接著我朋友 Jerry 在我前面丟了三個香蕉皮，我全部撞上，掉到第八名。大家都笑了，只有我笑不出來。比賽結束後，媽媽端來一盤水果：蘋果、柳丁和真的香蕉。Jerry 拿起一根香蕉說：「小心喔，別亂丟香蕉皮。」大家又笑了。我跟他說：「下週我會多練習，到時候打轉的就是你！」

passages.title: 傳統市場的水果阿嬤
passages.text: Every morning, Grandma Wang sells fruit at the traditional market near my home. Her stand is small, but it is always {1}. She knows which {2} is the sweetest in each season. In summer, she sells mangoes and {3}. In winter, she sells oranges and strawberries. She also has {4} all year round, because they grow in Taiwan in every season. My mom always buys from her because she never sells bad fruit. If something isn't fresh, she tells you so and doesn't sell it to you. "Grandma Wang is {5}," Mom says. "That's why everyone comes back to her." She has worked at this market for more than forty years. Last week, Grandma Wang gave me a free orange. "Study hard," she said. "And eat more fruit!"

blanks.why: 攤位很小，卻總是擠滿人 crowded。wooden（木製的）、national（國家的）、illegal（違法的）和「小卻…」的對比都不通。
她知道每一季哪一種水果 fruit 最甜。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都沒有甜度。
夏天賣芒果和葡萄 grapes。tickets（票）、letters（信）、offices（辦公室）都不是水果攤賣的東西。
台灣一年四季都有香蕉 bananas，所以她全年都賣。pockets（口袋）、villages（村莊）、museums（博物館）都不會「生長」。
不新鮮的水果她會直說、不賣給你，所以她很誠實 honest。careless（粗心的）、stupid（愚笨的）、rude（無禮的）都不是大家會一再回來的原因。

passages.zh: 每天早上，王阿嬤都在我家附近的傳統市場賣水果。她的攤位雖小，卻總是擠滿了人。她知道每一季哪種水果最甜：夏天賣芒果和葡萄，冬天賣柳丁和草莓。她一整年都有香蕉，因為台灣四季都長得出香蕉。媽媽總是跟她買，因為她從不賣壞掉的水果。如果東西不新鮮，她會直接告訴你，也不會賣給你。「王阿嬤很誠實，」媽媽說，「所以大家都會一直回來找她。」她在這個市場已經做了四十多年。上週，王阿嬤送我一顆柳丁。「好好讀書，」她說，「還有多吃水果！」

passages.title: 小小兵的香蕉蛋糕
passages.text: In the movie Despicable Me, the Minions are small, yellow, and very funny. They speak their own language, and their favorite food is {1}. When a Minion sees a banana, he goes {2} and forgets about his work. My little sister loves the Minions. For her birthday, Mom made her a Minion cake. The cake was yellow, and the eyes were made of {3} cut in half. Mom also put some {4} around the cake: bananas, of course! When my sister saw it, she was so happy that she {5} "Banana!" just like a Minion. She even wore yellow clothes and blue glasses. Then she sang a Minion song that nobody could understand. We all laughed. It was the yellowest birthday party ever.

blanks.why: 小小兵最愛吃的食物是香蕉 bananas。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、pockets（口袋）都不是食物。
go crazy「（興奮得）發狂」，看到香蕉就忘了工作。polite（有禮貌的）、honest（誠實的）、cheap（便宜的）都不能和 goes 搭配表示失控。
眼睛是用切半的葡萄 grapes 做的。tickets（票）、letters（信）、offices（辦公室）都不能切半放在蛋糕上。
在蛋糕旁邊擺水果 fruit，冒號後面說當然是香蕉。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能擺在蛋糕旁。
開心到像小小兵一樣大喊 shouted「Banana！」。spelled（拼字）、married（結婚）、borrowed（借）都不能表示興奮地喊叫。

passages.zh: 在電影《神偷奶爸》裡，小小兵又小又黃，非常好笑。牠們說自己的語言，最愛吃的食物是香蕉。小小兵一看到香蕉就會瘋掉，把工作全忘了。我妹妹很愛小小兵。她生日時，媽媽做了一個小小兵蛋糕，蛋糕是黃色的，眼睛是用切半的葡萄做的。媽媽還在蛋糕旁擺了一些水果──當然是香蕉！妹妹看到時開心得像小小兵一樣大喊「Banana！」，她甚至穿了黃衣服、戴藍色眼鏡，接著還唱了一首沒人聽得懂的小小兵歌。我們都笑了。那是史上最黃的生日派對。

passages.title: 學校的開心農場
passages.text: Our school has a small farm behind the gym. Each class has its own piece of land. This semester, our class decided to grow {1} like lettuce, carrots, and green beans. Our science teacher taught us how to make the soil rich. We took turns to {2} the plants every morning. Some bugs came and ate the leaves. We didn't want to use poison, so we sprayed {3} water on the leaves. It smelled nice, and the bugs went away. After two months, the lettuce was big and green. We used it to make salad for the whole class, with some cut {4} on top. Everyone agreed that the salad was {5}. Our teacher said, "Now you know how hard farmers work."

blanks.why: grow vegetables like lettuce, carrots, and green beans「種萵苣、紅蘿蔔、四季豆這些蔬菜」。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、letters（信）都不能種。
輪流每天早上檢查 check 植物。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）接 the plants 意思都不通。
lemon water「檸檬水」，噴在葉子上趕蟲。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不能做成水來噴。
沙拉上面放一些切好的水果 fruit。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能切、也不能放在沙拉上。
沙拉很好吃 delicious。honest（誠實的）、lonely（寂寞的）、careless（粗心的）都是形容人的，不能形容沙拉。

passages.zh: 我們學校的體育館後面有一座小農場，每一班都有自己的一塊地。這學期，我們班決定種萵苣、紅蘿蔔和四季豆等蔬菜。自然老師教我們怎麼讓土壤變肥沃。我們輪流在每天早上檢查植物。有些蟲跑來吃葉子，我們不想用農藥，就在葉子上噴檸檬水。聞起來很香，蟲也跑掉了。兩個月後，萵苣長得又大又綠。我們用它做了全班的沙拉，上面再放一些切好的水果。大家都同意那盤沙拉非常好吃。老師說：「現在你們知道農夫有多辛苦了吧。」

passages.title: 阿嬤的檸檬妙用
passages.text: Most people think a {1} is only for drinks. But it can do many things! My grandma uses {2} for almost everything. When the fridge smells bad, she cuts a lemon in half and puts it inside. When there are spots on her pots, she rubs them with lemon and salt. When I have a {3} throat, she makes me hot lemon tea with honey. She puts lemon juice on cut {4}, like apples, so it won't turn brown. She also squeezes lemon on fried fish and other {5} to make them taste fresh. Last week, I asked her, "Grandma, is there anything a lemon can't do?" She thought for a moment and laughed. "It can't make you stop asking questions!"

blanks.why: 大部分人以為檸檬 lemon 只能做飲料。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不能拿來做飲料。
阿嬤幾乎什麼都用檸檬 lemons，後面舉了很多例子。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、offices（辦公室）都不能切半放進冰箱。
sore throat「喉嚨痛」，所以喝熱檸檬蜂蜜茶。wooden（木製的）、national（國家的）、crowded（擁擠的）都不能形容喉嚨的症狀。
在切好的水果 fruit（例如蘋果）上擠檸檬汁，就不會變黑。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不會變褐色。
fried fish and other seafood「炸魚和其他海鮮」，擠檸檬讓它們吃起來更鮮。knowledge（知識）、information（資訊）、history（歷史）都不能吃。

passages.zh: 大多數人以為檸檬只能拿來做飲料，但它其實有很多用途！我阿嬤幾乎什麼事都用檸檬。冰箱有臭味時，她把一顆檸檬切半放進去；鍋子有污漬時，她用檸檬和鹽去搓。我喉嚨痛的時候，她會泡熱檸檬蜂蜜茶給我喝。她在切好的水果（像蘋果）上擠檸檬汁，水果就不會變黑。她也會在炸魚和其他海鮮上擠檸檬，讓它們吃起來更鮮。上週我問她：「阿嬤，有沒有什麼是檸檬做不到的？」她想了一下，笑著說：「它沒辦法讓你停止問問題！」

passages.title: 水果雕刻比賽
passages.text: Our school held a fruit carving contest last Friday. Each team had one hour to turn {1} into art. My team chose a big watermelon, and we wanted to carve it into a dragon. I was in charge of the eyes, and I used two black {2}. My friend Ben made the dragon's teeth from small pieces of apple. Another team made a boat out of a pineapple, with {3} as the people sitting on it. One girl carved a {4} into a tiny yellow rose. It was so small and {5} that everyone took photos of it. She won first place. In the end, our dragon won second place, and we were very happy. After the contest, we did one more thing together: we ate all the art. It was the most delicious contest ever.

blanks.why: turn fruit into art「把水果變成藝術品」，這是水果雕刻比賽。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能拿來雕刻。
用兩顆黑葡萄 grapes 當龍的眼睛。tickets（票）、letters（信）、offices（辦公室）都不能放在西瓜上當眼睛。
用香蕉 bananas 當坐在鳳梨船上的人。pockets（口袋）、villages（村莊）、museums（博物館）都不是水果，不能雕成小人。
把一顆檸檬 lemon 雕成黃色的小玫瑰。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、corner（角落）都不能雕、也不是黃色的水果。
so small and beautiful that…「又小又漂亮，所以大家都拍照」。crowded（擁擠的）、national（國家的）、illegal（違法的）都不能說明大家為什麼拍照。

passages.zh: 上週五，我們學校舉辦了水果雕刻比賽。每一組有一個小時，把水果變成藝術品。我們這組選了一顆大西瓜，想把它雕成一條龍。我負責眼睛，用了兩顆黑葡萄。我朋友 Ben 用小塊蘋果做龍的牙齒。另一組用鳳梨做成一艘船，用香蕉當坐在船上的人。有個女生把一顆檸檬雕成一朵黃色的小玫瑰，又小又漂亮，每個人都拍照，她得了第一名。最後，我們的龍得了第二名，我們都很開心。比賽結束後，我們一起做了最後一件事：把所有藝術品都吃掉。那是史上最好吃的比賽。

passages.title: 颱風過後的菜價
passages.text: After a strong typhoon hit Taiwan last summer, many farms were badly damaged. The heavy rain washed away a lot of {1} in the fields. A few days later, Mom came back from the market with a surprised face. "One cabbage costs three hundred dollars now!" she said. Before the typhoon, it was only fifty. The price of {2} went up, too, because many {3} fell from the trees in the strong wind. Mom said we had to {4} money for a few weeks. So we ate more eggs, tofu, and bean sprouts, which were still cheap. Dad even made a {5} drink with fruit from our neighbor's tree instead of buying juice. Two weeks later, prices went back to normal. When Mom bought cabbage again, she said, "Now I know how much farmers do for us."

blanks.why: 大雨沖走田裡很多蔬菜 vegetables，後面說高麗菜變貴。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、letters（信）都不會長在田裡。
the price of fruit「水果的價格」也上漲。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不是在市場買賣、有價格的東西。
很多香蕉 bananas 被強風從樹上吹落。pockets（口袋）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不會長在樹上。
save money「省錢」，菜價太貴，只好吃便宜的東西。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）接 money 都不通。
a lemon drink「檸檬飲料」，用鄰居家樹上的果實做。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、corner（角落）都不能做成飲料。

passages.zh: 去年夏天一個強颱侵襲台灣之後，很多農場都受到嚴重損壞，大雨沖走了田裡很多蔬菜。幾天後，媽媽從市場回來，一臉驚訝。「一顆高麗菜現在要三百元！」她說。颱風前，一顆只要五十元。水果的價格也漲了，因為很多香蕉被強風從樹上吹落。媽媽說，我們這幾週得省點錢。所以我們多吃蛋、豆腐和豆芽菜，因為這些還是很便宜。爸爸甚至用鄰居家樹上的果子做了檸檬飲料，而不去買果汁。兩週後，價格恢復正常。媽媽再次買高麗菜時說：「現在我知道農夫為我們付出了多少。」

passages.title: 阿嬤拜拜的水果
passages.text: During Chinese New Year, my grandma goes to the temple to pray. She always brings a big plate of {1}. Her favorite is the pineapple, because in Taiwanese its name sounds like "good luck is coming." She also brings oranges, apples, and a bunch of {2}, because a bunch has many small fruits, which means a big, happy family. But she never brings guavas. Some people believe guavas are not clean enough for the gods. "We must be {3} to the gods," Grandma says. After praying, we take the fruit home and eat it. Grandma says the gods have already enjoyed the smell, so now we can {4} the taste. Last year, I asked if I could bring a {5} for the gods, too, because I love bananas. Grandma laughed. "You just want to eat it later!"

blanks.why: a big plate of fruit「一大盤水果」，後面提到鳳梨、柳丁、蘋果。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能裝盤拜拜。
a bunch of grapes「一串葡萄」，一串有很多顆，代表大家庭。tickets（票）、letters（信）、offices（辦公室）都不能說「一串、很多小果實」。
be polite to…「對…有禮貌」，所以不帶不夠乾淨的芭樂。wooden（木製的）、crowded（擁擠的）、thirsty（口渴的）都不能接 to the gods 表示態度。
enjoy the taste「享用味道」，和前面神明 enjoyed the smell 對應。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、lend（借出）接 the taste 都不通。
帶一根香蕉 banana 去拜，因為我愛吃香蕉。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不能吃。

passages.zh: 每到農曆新年，阿嬤都會去廟裡拜拜，她總是帶一大盤水果。她最喜歡鳳梨，因為台語唸起來像「旺來」。她也會帶柳丁、蘋果和一串葡萄，因為一串有很多小果實，代表一個快樂的大家庭。但她從來不帶芭樂，有些人認為芭樂不夠乾淨，不適合拜神。「對神明要有禮貌。」阿嬤說。拜完之後，我們把水果帶回家吃。阿嬤說神明已經享用過香味了，現在換我們享用味道。去年，我問阿嬤可不可以也帶一根香蕉拜神，因為我很愛吃香蕉。阿嬤笑著說：「你只是想等一下自己吃吧！」

passages.title: 第一次吃榴槤
passages.text: My dad went on a business trip to Thailand and brought back a strange {1}. It was big, green, and covered with sharp spikes. "This is a durian," he said. "People call it the king of fruits." When he opened it, a strong {2} filled the whole kitchen. My sister ran away and held her nose. "It smells like old socks!" she shouted. But Dad said, "Just try it." I was {3}, but I took a small bite. It was soft and sweet, like cream! It was nothing like {4} or {5}. I had never tasted anything like it before. I ate three pieces, and Dad ate the rest. Now durian is one of my favorite fruits. But Mom has a new rule: we can only eat it outside on the balcony.

blanks.why: a strange fruit「一種奇怪的水果」，後面說它是水果之王榴槤。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能從國外帶回來、也沒有刺。
a strong smell filled the kitchen「一股濃烈的氣味充滿廚房」，妹妹還捏住鼻子。ticket（票）、uniform（制服）、corner（角落）都不能「充滿廚房」。
第一次吃很緊張 nervous，但還是咬了一口。wooden（木製的）、crowded（擁擠的）、national（國家的）都不能形容人的心情。
nothing like bananas「和香蕉完全不同」。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、pockets（口袋）都不是能拿來比較味道的水果。
nothing like … grapes「和葡萄完全不同」。letters（信）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不是能拿來比較味道的水果。

passages.zh: 爸爸去泰國出差，帶回來一種奇怪的水果。它又大又綠，全身都是尖刺。「這是榴槤，」他說，「大家叫它水果之王。」他一打開，一股濃烈的氣味就充滿整個廚房。妹妹捏著鼻子跑走，大喊：「聞起來像舊襪子！」但爸爸說：「吃吃看嘛。」我很緊張，但還是咬了一小口。它又軟又甜，像奶油一樣！和香蕉或葡萄完全不同，我從來沒吃過這種味道。我吃了三塊，剩下的爸爸吃掉了。現在榴槤是我最喜歡的水果之一。不過媽媽訂了新規定：我們只能到陽台上吃。

passages.title: 大猩猩的生日蛋糕
passages.text: Last Saturday was the birthday of Bobo, the oldest gorilla at the zoo. He turned forty-five! The zookeepers made him a special cake. It wasn't made of flour or sugar. Instead, it was made of ice, {1}, and lots of fruit. On top, there were {2}, his favorite, and a big "45" made of red {3}. Many visitors came to {4} with him. When the cake was put in his area, Bobo walked over slowly. He looked at it, picked up a banana, and ate it. Then he sat down and ate the grapes one by one. The children cheered. A zookeeper said, "Gorillas eat a lot of plants and {5} in the wild. This cake is healthy for him." Bobo finished everything, and then he lay down for a long nap.

blanks.why: 蛋糕是用冰塊、蔬菜 vegetables 和很多水果做的。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、letters（信）都不能做成給動物吃的蛋糕。
上面放著牠最愛的香蕉 bananas，後面也說牠拿起一根香蕉。pockets（口袋）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不能吃。
用紅葡萄 grapes 排成「45」，後面說牠一顆顆吃掉葡萄。tickets（票）、corners（角落）、uniforms（制服）都不能一顆顆吃。
celebrate with him「和牠一起慶祝」生日。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）都不是來參加生日的目的。
大猩猩在野外吃很多植物和水果 fruit。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能吃。

passages.zh: 上週六是動物園裡最老的大猩猩 Bobo 的生日，牠滿四十五歲了！管理員為牠做了一個特別的蛋糕。蛋糕不是用麵粉和糖做的，而是用冰塊、蔬菜和很多水果做的。上面放著牠最愛的香蕉，還有用紅葡萄排成的大大的「45」。很多遊客都來和牠一起慶祝。蛋糕放進牠的活動區時，Bobo 慢慢走過去，看了看，拿起一根香蕉吃掉，接著坐下來一顆一顆地吃葡萄。小朋友們都歡呼起來。一位管理員說：「大猩猩在野外會吃很多植物和水果，這個蛋糕對牠很健康。」Bobo 把蛋糕全吃光，然後躺下來睡了一場長長的午覺。

passages.title: 自己做水果冰棒
passages.text: It was the hottest day of summer, and the ice cream shop was too far away. So my cousin and I decided to make our own popsicles. First, we cut some {1} into small pieces: mangoes, kiwis, and {2}. Then we put the pieces into plastic cups. My cousin added some honey and {3} juice to a bottle of apple juice and {4} it well. We poured the juice into the cups and put a stick in each one. Then we put them in the freezer and waited. Every thirty minutes, my cousin opened the freezer to check. "Stop it! They will never get hard that way," I said. Four hours later, the popsicles were finally ready. They were colorful and sweet, and we were so {5} of them. We gave one to everyone in the family.

blanks.why: cut some fruit into small pieces「把一些水果切小塊」，冒號後面列出芒果、奇異果和葡萄。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能切。
mangoes, kiwis, and grapes「芒果、奇異果和葡萄」，都是水果。tickets（票）、letters（信）、offices（辦公室）都不能切塊做冰棒。
lemon juice「檸檬汁」，和蜂蜜一起加進蘋果汁。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、corner（角落）都不能做成汁。
mix it well「攪拌均勻」，mix 的過去式 mixed。spelled（拼字）、married（結婚）、prayed（禱告）都不能用在果汁上。
be proud of…「以…為傲」，對自己做的冰棒很得意。wooden（木製的）、crowded（擁擠的）、thirsty（口渴的）都不能和 of them 搭配表示心情。

passages.zh: 那是夏天最熱的一天，冰淇淋店又太遠，所以我和表哥決定自己做冰棒。首先，我們把一些水果切成小塊：芒果、奇異果和葡萄，再把水果放進塑膠杯裡。表哥在一瓶蘋果汁裡加了蜂蜜和檸檬汁，攪拌均勻。我們把果汁倒進杯子，每杯插一根棒子，再放進冷凍庫等待。表哥每三十分鐘就打開冷凍庫看一次。「別再開了！這樣永遠都不會結冰啦。」我說。四個小時後，冰棒終於做好了，五顏六色又甜甜的，我們好得意。我們給家裡每個人都送了一支。

passages.title: 果汁店的機器人
passages.text: A new juice shop near my school has a robot that makes drinks. You choose what you want on a screen, and the robot does the rest. Yesterday, I {1} a banana milk. The robot picked up a {2}, took off the peel, and put it into the blender with milk. It took only one minute! My friend Ivy wanted something sour, so she chose {3} green tea. Then my friend Leo tried to be funny. He pressed every button and chose seven kinds of {4} for one drink. The robot stopped for a moment. Its screen said, "Are you sure?" Leo pressed "Yes." The drink came out brown and thick. Leo took a sip and made a face. "It tastes {5}," he said. The robot's screen showed a smiling face and the words "I told you so."

blanks.why: order「點（飲料）」，order 的過去式 ordered。spelled（拼字）、married（結婚）、prayed（禱告）接 a banana milk 都不通。
機器人拿起一根香蕉 banana，剝皮後放進果汁機。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不能剝皮打成果汁。
想喝酸的，所以選檸檬 lemon 綠茶。ticket（票）、corner（角落）、uniform（制服）都不能加進綠茶，也不是酸的。
seven kinds of fruit「七種水果」打成一杯。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能放進飲料。
taste terrible「味道很糟」，他喝了一口就皺眉。wooden（木製的）、national（國家的）、crowded（擁擠的）都不能形容味道。

passages.zh: 我學校附近新開了一家果汁店，店裡有一個會做飲料的機器人。你在螢幕上選好想喝的，剩下的就交給機器人。昨天，我點了香蕉牛奶。機器人拿起一根香蕉，剝掉皮，和牛奶一起放進果汁機，只花了一分鐘！我朋友 Ivy 想喝酸的，所以選了檸檬綠茶。接著我朋友 Leo 想搞笑，他把每個按鈕都按了，在一杯飲料裡選了七種水果。機器人停頓了一下，螢幕上出現「你確定嗎？」Leo 按了「是」。做出來的飲料又褐又稠。Leo 喝了一口，臉都皺起來了。「好難喝。」他說。機器人的螢幕上出現一張笑臉和一行字：「我早就跟你說了。」

passages.title: 教練的檸檬
passages.text: Our school basketball team lost the final game by one point. In the locker room, everyone was quiet, and some players were crying. Then Coach Lin came in with a bag of {1}. We didn't understand. He put one in each player's hand. "Taste it," he said. We each took a bite. It was so sour that we all made funny faces, and some of us started to {2}. Coach Lin smiled. "Life will give you lemons sometimes," he said. "Losing a game is a lemon. But you can add water and sugar and make lemonade. That means you learn from your {3} and become better." The next week, we practiced harder than ever. And after every game, win or lose, Coach Lin gave us a cup of {4} juice and a bag of {5} on the bus home.

blanks.why: a bag of lemons「一袋檸檬」，後面叫大家咬一口、很酸。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、pockets（口袋）都不能吃。
酸到做鬼臉，有些人開始笑 laugh 了出來。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）都不是看到彼此鬼臉的反應。
learn from your mistakes「從錯誤中學習」。tickets（票）、corners（角落）、uniforms（制服）都不能從中學到教訓。
a cup of lemon juice「一杯檸檬汁」，呼應前面的檸檬比喻。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不能做成汁。
a bag of fruit「一袋水果」，比賽後的點心。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能裝在袋子裡給球員吃。

passages.zh: 我們學校籃球隊在決賽以一分之差輸了。更衣室裡大家都很安靜，有些隊員在哭。這時林教練拿著一袋檸檬走進來，我們都不懂他要做什麼。他在每個隊員手上放一顆檸檬，說：「嚐嚐看。」我們每個人咬了一口，酸到大家都做出好笑的鬼臉，有些人開始笑了出來。林教練笑著說：「人生有時候會給你檸檬。輸掉比賽就是一顆檸檬，但你可以加水和糖，做成檸檬水。意思是，你要從錯誤中學習，讓自己變得更好。」接下來那週，我們練得比以前更努力。而且之後每場比賽，不論輸贏，林教練都會在回程的巴士上給我們一杯檸檬汁和一袋水果。

passages.title: 香蕉王國的回憶
passages.text: Did you know that Taiwan was once called the "Kingdom of Bananas"? About sixty years ago, Taiwan sold a lot of {1} to Japan. My grandpa was a banana farmer in Kaohsiung back then. He told me the work was very {2}. The bananas had to be picked before they were ripe. Then workers {3} them into boxes and sent them to the harbor. The trip to Japan took many days on a ship. When the bananas arrived, they turned yellow and sweet. Japanese people loved Taiwanese bananas because of their rich taste, and farmers made good money. Today, Taiwan still grows many kinds of {4}, like mangoes, pineapples, and {5}. But for Grandpa, the banana is still the king. "Every banana has a story," he says.

blanks.why: 台灣當年賣很多香蕉 bananas 到日本，所以叫「香蕉王國」。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、offices（辦公室）都不能外銷、也不會被種植。
the work was very hard「工作很辛苦」。wooden（木製的）、national（國家的）、crowded（擁擠的）都不能形容工作的辛苦。
pack them into boxes「把它們裝箱」，pack 的過去式 packed。spelled（拼字）、married（結婚）、prayed（禱告）接 into boxes 都不通。
many kinds of fruit「很多種水果」，後面舉了芒果、鳳梨、葡萄。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能種植。
芒果、鳳梨和葡萄 grapes 都是台灣種的水果。tickets（票）、letters（信）、pockets（口袋）都不能種。

passages.zh: 你知道台灣曾經被稱為「香蕉王國」嗎？大約六十年前，台灣賣了大量香蕉到日本。我爺爺當時是高雄的蕉農，他告訴我那份工作非常辛苦。香蕉必須在成熟前就採下來，接著工人把它們裝箱，運到港口。到日本要坐好幾天的船。香蕉送到時，就變得又黃又甜。日本人很喜歡台灣香蕉濃郁的味道，農民也賺了不少錢。現在台灣仍然種很多種水果，像是芒果、鳳梨和葡萄。但對爺爺來說，香蕉永遠是王。「每一根香蕉都有一個故事。」他說。

passages.title: 葡萄乾的祕密
passages.text: My little sister asked me a question at breakfast. She was eating cereal with raisins. "Where do raisins come from? Do they grow on trees?" I laughed. "No, raisins are dried {1}." She didn't believe me, so we did an experiment. We washed some green grapes and put them on a plate by the sunny window. Every day, we {2} them. After a week, they became small, brown, and soft. My sister took one and tasted it. "It's a raisin!" she shouted. "It's even sweeter than before!" I explained that the water in the {3} goes away, but the sugar stays. Then she wanted to dry everything. She tried a {4}, an apple, and even a {5}. The banana and apple chips were great, but the dried lemon was too sour. "Some fruit should just stay the way it is," she said.

blanks.why: raisins are dried grapes「葡萄乾就是曬乾的葡萄」，後面她們真的曬了葡萄。tickets（票）、letters（信）、offices（辦公室）曬乾都不會變成葡萄乾。
每天檢查 checked 葡萄的變化。spelled（拼字）、married（結婚）、prayed（禱告）接 them 都不通。
水果 fruit 裡的水分不見了，糖分留下來，所以更甜。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）裡面都沒有水分和糖。
試著曬一根香蕉 banana，後面說香蕉乾很好吃。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不能曬乾來吃。
甚至曬了一顆檸檬 lemon，結果太酸。corner（角落）、uniform（制服）、museum（博物館）都不會「太酸」。

passages.zh: 妹妹在吃早餐時問了我一個問題。她正在吃加了葡萄乾的穀片。「葡萄乾是從哪裡來的？長在樹上嗎？」我笑了：「不是啦，葡萄乾就是曬乾的葡萄。」她不相信，所以我們做了一個實驗。我們洗了一些綠葡萄，放在盤子上，擺在有陽光的窗邊，每天都去檢查。一星期後，葡萄變得又小、又褐、又軟。妹妹拿起一顆嚐嚐。「是葡萄乾耶！」她大叫，「比原本還甜！」我解釋說，水果裡的水分會不見，但糖分會留下來。接著她什麼都想曬乾，試了香蕉、蘋果，甚至還有檸檬。香蕉乾和蘋果乾都很好吃，但檸檬乾太酸了。「有些水果還是保持原樣就好。」她說。

passages.title: 動物森友會的水果島
passages.text: In the game Animal Crossing, you live on an island with cute animal neighbors. When you start the game, your island has only one kind of {1}. Mine had cherries. To get other kinds, you have to visit your friends' islands or ask your neighbors. My friend Amy's island had oranges, so she {2} me some in the mail. I planted them, and soon I had orange trees, too. Later, I found coconuts on a beach. They are not {3}, but they grow on palm trees by the sea, too. In the newer version of the game, you can also grow {4} like pumpkins and tomatoes. My favorite thing is selling fruit. Fruit from other islands sells for a higher price, so I made a lot of money. Now I {5} the biggest house on my island.

blanks.why: 島上一開始只有一種水果 fruit，我的是櫻桃。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不會長在樹上，也沒有種類之分。
send + 人 + 東西「寄給某人」，send 的過去式 sent。spelled（拼字）、married（結婚）、prayed（禱告）都不能接 me some in the mail。
椰子不是香蕉 bananas，但也長在海邊的棕櫚樹上。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、pockets（口袋）都不會長在樹上。
grow vegetables like pumpkins and tomatoes「種南瓜、番茄這些蔬菜」。letters（信）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不能種。
own「擁有」，賺了很多錢後擁有島上最大的房子。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）接 the biggest house 都不通。

passages.zh: 在遊戲《動物森友會》裡，你住在一座小島上，鄰居都是可愛的動物。遊戲一開始，你的島上只有一種水果，我的是櫻桃。想要其他種類，就得去朋友的島上，或是問問鄰居。我朋友 Amy 的島上有柳丁，所以她用郵件寄了一些給我。我把它們種下去，很快就有了柳丁樹。後來我在海灘上撿到椰子，它們不是香蕉，但也長在海邊的棕櫚樹上。在比較新的版本裡，還可以種南瓜、番茄這些蔬菜。我最喜歡賣水果，因為別的島的水果可以賣比較高的價錢，所以我賺了很多錢。現在我擁有島上最大的房子。

passages.title: 太空站裡的蔬菜
passages.text: Astronauts on the International Space Station usually eat food from bags and cans. Fresh {1} are hard to find in space. But in 2015, astronauts did something special. They grew lettuce in a small box with red and blue lights. Then they {2} it for the first time. "It's fresh and crunchy!" one of them said. Since then, they have grown other plants, like tomatoes and chili peppers. Scientists hope that one day people on Mars can grow their own {3}, too. Maybe they will grow {4} or {5} under the red Mars sky. It sounds like a dream, but many people are working hard to make it real. Maybe someday you will eat a salad that was grown on another planet!

blanks.why: 新鮮的蔬菜 vegetables 在太空很難找到，後面說他們種了萵苣。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、letters（信）都不能用「新鮮」來形容、也不能種。
taste「嚐」，第一次嚐自己種的萵苣，taste 的過去式 tasted。spelled（拼字）、married（結婚）、prayed（禱告）接 it（萵苣）都不通。
grow their own fruit「種自己的水果」。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能種植。
在火星的天空下種香蕉 bananas。pockets（口袋）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不能種植。
或是種葡萄 grapes。tickets（票）、corners（角落）、uniforms（制服）都不能種植。

passages.zh: 國際太空站上的太空人通常吃袋裝和罐裝的食物，在太空中很難吃到新鮮的蔬菜。但在 2015 年，太空人做了一件特別的事：他們在一個有紅光和藍光的小箱子裡種出萵苣，然後第一次嚐了自己種的菜。「又新鮮又脆！」其中一位說。從那之後，他們又種了其他植物，像是番茄和辣椒。科學家希望有一天，在火星上的人也能種自己的水果，也許他們會在火星紅色的天空下種香蕉或葡萄。這聽起來像一場夢，但很多人正努力讓它成真。說不定有一天，你會吃到在另一個星球上種出來的沙拉！

passages.title: 彩虹餐盤
passages.text: In health class, our teacher showed us a picture of a "rainbow plate." "Try to eat {1} and fruit of many different colors every day," she said. "Each color {2} your body in a different way." Red tomatoes are good for your heart. Orange carrots help your eyes. Yellow {3} give you energy. Green broccoli makes your bones strong, and purple {4} are good for your brain. Then she gave us homework: take a photo of one meal with five colors. At home, I found red, orange, yellow, and green food, but nothing purple. Then I saw an eggplant in the fridge. Mom helped me cook it with garlic. My plate looked like a rainbow, and I felt very {5} after eating it. I got an A on my homework, too!

blanks.why: eat vegetables and fruit「吃蔬菜和水果」。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、letters（信）都不能吃、也沒有顏色之分的營養。
protect your body「保護你的身體」。spells（拼字）、marries（結婚）、prays（禱告）接 your body 都不通。
黃色的香蕉 bananas 給你能量。pockets（口袋）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不能吃、也不是黃色的食物。
紫色的葡萄 grapes 對大腦好。tickets（票）、corners（角落）、uniforms（制服）都不能吃。
feel healthy「覺得很健康」，吃完彩虹餐盤之後。wooden（木製的）、crowded（擁擠的）、national（國家的）都不能形容身體的感覺。

passages.zh: 健康課時，老師給我們看一張「彩虹餐盤」的圖片。「每天試著吃很多種不同顏色的蔬菜和水果，」她說，「每種顏色用不同的方式保護你的身體。」紅色番茄對心臟好，橘色紅蘿蔔對眼睛好，黃色香蕉給你能量，綠色花椰菜讓骨頭強壯，紫色葡萄對大腦好。接著她出了一項作業：拍一張有五種顏色的餐點照片。回到家，我找到紅色、橘色、黃色和綠色的食物，就是沒有紫色。後來我在冰箱裡看到一條茄子，媽媽幫我用蒜頭炒了它。我的盤子看起來就像一道彩虹，吃完覺得很健康。我的作業也拿了 A！

passages.title: 教室裡消失的香蕉
passages.text: Every morning, our teacher Mr. Chen puts a {1} on his desk for breakfast. But last Monday, it was gone! "Who took my banana?" he asked. Nobody answered. On Tuesday, his {2} disappeared, too. Our class decided to {3} the mystery. Jenny, who loves detective stories, put a small camera behind the bookshelf. On Wednesday, Mr. Chen left a {4} and an apple on his desk as a test. At lunchtime, we watched the video together. A small brown bird flew in through the window, looked at the lemon, and flew away. Then it came back and took a piece of apple! Everyone laughed. "So the thief is a bird," Mr. Chen said. "Maybe it doesn't like sour {5}." From then on, he kept his breakfast in a box.

blanks.why: 老師每天放一根香蕉 banana 在桌上當早餐，後面他問「誰拿了我的香蕉」。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、letter（信）都不能當早餐。
星期二換葡萄 grapes 不見了。tickets（票）、corners（角落）、uniforms（制服）都不是早餐、也不會被鳥叼走。
solve the mystery「解開謎團」。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）接 the mystery 都不通。
放一顆檸檬 lemon 和一顆蘋果當測試，後面說鳥看了檸檬就飛走。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不是水果，和後面「酸的水果」不合。
sour fruit「酸的水果」，指檸檬。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都沒有酸味。

passages.zh: 每天早上，陳老師都會在桌上放一根香蕉當早餐。但上週一，香蕉不見了！「誰拿了我的香蕉？」他問。沒有人回答。星期二，他的葡萄也不見了。我們班決定要解開這個謎團。熱愛偵探故事的 Jenny 在書架後面放了一台小攝影機。星期三，陳老師在桌上放了一顆檸檬和一顆蘋果當作測試。午餐時間，我們一起看影片：一隻褐色的小鳥從窗戶飛進來，看了看檸檬就飛走了，接著又飛回來叼走一塊蘋果！大家都笑了。「原來小偷是一隻鳥，」陳老師說，「也許牠不喜歡酸的水果。」從那以後，他都把早餐放在盒子裡。

passages.title: 日本交換生的水果驚奇
passages.text: Yuki, an exchange student from Japan, stayed with my family for a month. In Japan, {1} is often very expensive. One nice melon can cost more than a thousand Taiwan dollars! So when we took her to the market, she was very {2}. A big bunch of {3} was only sixty dollars. She also bought a box of {4} from Changhua for two hundred dollars. She tried many fruits for the first time, like dragon fruit, wax apples, and lychees. "In Japan, I only see these in pictures!" she said. Every night after dinner, Mom cut a plate of fruit for us, and Yuki ate more than anyone. On her last day, she hugged us and said, "I'll miss your family. And I'll {5} Taiwanese fruit, too!"

blanks.why: 在日本，水果 fruit 常常很貴，後面舉哈密瓜為例。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都沒有價格。
台灣水果便宜，所以她很驚訝 surprised。wooden（木製的）、crowded（擁擠的）、national（國家的）都不能形容人的反應。
a big bunch of bananas「一大串香蕉」只要六十元。pockets（口袋）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不能說「一串」、也不在市場賣。
a box of grapes from Changhua「一箱彰化葡萄」。tickets（票）、letters（信）、corners（角落）都不是彰化有名的農產品。
miss「想念」，前面也說會想念我們家。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）接 Taiwanese fruit 都不通。

passages.zh: 來自日本的交換學生 Yuki 在我們家住了一個月。在日本，水果常常很貴，一顆好的哈密瓜可能超過一千台幣！所以我們帶她去市場時，她非常驚訝：一大串香蕉只要六十元。她還花兩百元買了一箱彰化葡萄。她第一次吃到很多水果，像是火龍果、蓮霧和荔枝。「在日本，這些我只在圖片上看過！」她說。每天晚餐後，媽媽都會切一盤水果給我們，Yuki 吃得比誰都多。最後一天，她抱著我們說：「我會想念你們一家人，也會想念台灣的水果！」

passages.title: 狗狗不能吃葡萄
passages.text: Last weekend, my dog Lucky got very sick. On Saturday morning, he ate some {1} that fell on the kitchen floor. I didn't think it was a big deal. But in the afternoon, Lucky started to throw up, and he didn't want to move. We took him to the animal hospital right away. The doctor said, "Grapes are very {2} for dogs. Even a few can hurt their kidneys." She gave Lucky some medicine and kept him at the hospital for two days. Luckily, he got better. The doctor also told us that dogs shouldn't eat chocolate, onions, or raisins. "But some {3} is fine," she said. "A little piece of apple or {4} is a good snack." Now we keep all food off the floor. When Lucky learns a new trick, he gets a small slice of banana as a {5}.

blanks.why: 狗吃了掉在廚房地上的葡萄 grapes，後面醫生說葡萄對狗很危險。tickets（票）、letters（信）、offices（辦公室）都不能吃。
dangerous for dogs「對狗很危險」，連幾顆都會傷害腎臟。wooden（木製的）、crowded（擁擠的）、national（國家的）都不能說明對狗的影響。
有些水果 fruit 狗可以吃，後面舉蘋果和香蕉為例。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能給狗吃。
一小塊蘋果或香蕉 banana 是不錯的點心。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不能吃。
as a prize「當作獎勵」，學會新把戲就給一片香蕉。ticket（票）、corner（角落）、uniform（制服）都不能表示獎勵。

passages.zh: 上週末，我的狗 Lucky 病得很重。星期六早上，牠吃了掉在廚房地上的葡萄。我以為沒什麼大不了，但到了下午，Lucky 開始嘔吐，也不想動。我們馬上帶牠去動物醫院。醫生說：「葡萄對狗非常危險，就算只吃幾顆也可能傷到腎臟。」她給 Lucky 吃藥，讓牠在醫院住了兩天。幸好牠好起來了。醫生還告訴我們，狗不能吃巧克力、洋蔥或葡萄乾。「不過有些水果沒問題，」她說，「一小塊蘋果或香蕉就是很好的點心。」現在我們不會讓任何食物留在地上。每次 Lucky 學會一個新把戲，就能得到一小片香蕉當獎勵。

passages.title: 檸檬臉挑戰
passages.text: Last week, a funny video became popular at our school. It was called the "Lemon Face Challenge." In the video, people put a slice of {1} in their mouth and try not to make a face. My friends and I wanted to {2} it, too. We bought some lemons and cut them into slices. Kevin went first. "This is easy," he said. But one second later, his eyes closed, and his whole face looked like a crushed paper ball. We laughed so hard. Next was Lily. She kept her face still for ten seconds and won the game. "How did you do that?" we asked. She smiled. "My grandma makes me eat sour {3} all the time." After the challenge, our mouths needed something sweet, so we went to the store to buy some {4} and {5}.

blanks.why: a slice of lemon「一片檸檬」，放進嘴裡試著不做鬼臉。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不能切片放進嘴裡。
try it「試試看」這個挑戰。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）接 it（挑戰）都不通。
sour fruit「酸的水果」，奶奶常叫她吃，所以她不怕酸。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能吃、也不會酸。
嘴巴想吃甜的，所以去買香蕉 bananas。pockets（口袋）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不能吃。
和香蕉一起買的葡萄 grapes。letters（信）、corners（角落）、uniforms（制服）都不是甜的食物。

passages.zh: 上週，一支好笑的影片在我們學校爆紅，叫做「檸檬臉挑戰」。影片裡，大家把一片檸檬放進嘴裡，試著不做鬼臉。我和朋友們也想試試看。我們買了一些檸檬，切成片。Kevin 先來。「這很簡單。」他說。但一秒後，他的眼睛就閉起來，整張臉皺得像一顆被捏扁的紙球。我們笑翻了。接著輪到 Lily，她的臉十秒鐘都沒動，贏得了比賽。「你怎麼做到的？」我們問。她笑著說：「我阿嬤常常叫我吃酸的水果。」挑戰結束後，我們的嘴巴需要一點甜的東西，所以就去商店買了一些香蕉和葡萄。

passages.title: 水果國王選舉
passages.text: In the Kingdom of the Kitchen, the fruits decided to choose a new king. Many fruits wanted the job. The apple said, "I am red and {1}. Everyone eats me." The {2} said, "I give people energy, and I'm easy to carry." The {3} said, "I am sour, but I make every drink and dish better." Then a bunch of {4} said, "We are a team. Vote for all of us!" The {5} were watching from the fridge. "Why only fruit?" asked the carrot. "We are good for people, too!" The fruits talked for a long time. In the end, they decided to share the crown with the carrot, the cabbage, and the tomato. "Together, we make people healthy," they said. And everyone in the kitchen lived happily ever after.

blanks.why: 蘋果說自己又紅又受歡迎 popular，所以大家都吃它。wooden（木製的）、crowded（擁擠的）、national（國家的）都不能說明大家為什麼都吃它。
香蕉 banana 說自己給人能量、又方便攜帶。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不是水果，不能參加水果選舉。
檸檬 lemon 說自己雖酸，卻能讓每道飲料和菜更好吃。ticket（票）、corner（角落）、uniform（制服）都不是酸的水果。
a bunch of grapes「一串葡萄」，所以說「我們是一個團隊」。tickets（票）、letters（信）、offices（辦公室）都不能說「一串」、也不是水果。
從冰箱裡看的是蔬菜 vegetables，後面紅蘿蔔說話。letters（信）、museums（博物館）、offices（辦公室）都不會放在冰箱裡。

passages.zh: 在廚房王國裡，水果們決定選出一位新國王，很多水果都想當。蘋果說：「我又紅又受歡迎，大家都吃我。」香蕉說：「我能給人能量，而且很方便攜帶。」檸檬說：「我雖然酸，但能讓每一杯飲料、每一道菜變得更好吃。」接著一串葡萄說：「我們是一個團隊，請投給我們全部！」蔬菜們在冰箱裡看著。「為什麼只有水果？」紅蘿蔔問，「我們對人也很好啊！」水果們討論了很久，最後決定和紅蘿蔔、高麗菜、番茄一起分享王冠。「我們一起讓人們健康。」他們說。從此以後，廚房裡的大家都過著幸福快樂的日子。

passages.title: 便利商店的一根香蕉
passages.text: In Taiwan, you can buy a single banana at many convenience stores. My grandma loves this. She lives alone, and a whole bunch of {1} is too much for her. "Before, I always had to throw half of them away," she said. "It was such a {2}." Now she buys one banana every morning when she gets her newspaper. It is cheap, {3}, and healthy. The stores also sell cut {4} in small boxes, like pineapple and guava. Some even sell salads with fresh {5} for office workers who are too busy to cook. Grandma says, "When I was young, small shops only sold candy and cigarettes. Now they sell healthy food. Taiwan has changed a lot!" Then she peeled her banana and ate it happily on the way home.

blanks.why: a whole bunch of bananas「一整串香蕉」，對獨居的阿嬤來說太多了。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、pockets（口袋）都不能說「一串」、也不會吃不完。
such a waste「真是浪費」，以前常吃不完要丟掉一半。ticket（票）、corner（角落）、uniform（制服）都不能形容把食物丟掉這件事。
便宜、方便 convenient 又健康。wooden（木製的）、national（國家的）、honest（誠實的）都不能形容在超商買香蕉這件事。
cut fruit in small boxes「小盒裝的切好水果」，例如鳳梨和芭樂。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能切、也不能裝盒賣。
salads with fresh vegetables「有新鮮蔬菜的沙拉」。letters（信）、offices（辦公室）、museums（博物館）都不能做成沙拉。

passages.zh: 在台灣，很多便利商店都可以只買一根香蕉。我阿嬤很喜歡這樣。她一個人住，一整串香蕉對她來說太多了。「以前我總是要丟掉一半，」她說，「真是浪費。」現在她每天早上去買報紙時，就順便買一根香蕉，便宜、方便又健康。超商也賣小盒裝的切好水果，像鳳梨和芭樂，有些甚至賣有新鮮蔬菜的沙拉，給忙到沒時間煮飯的上班族。阿嬤說：「我年輕的時候，小店只賣糖果和香菸，現在都賣健康的食物了，台灣變了好多！」說完，她剝開香蕉，在回家的路上開心地吃了起來。

passages.title: 媽媽的綠色蔬果汁
passages.text: Every morning, my mom makes a big green drink in the blender. She puts in spinach, celery, and other green {1}. Then she adds a {2} to make it sweet and some {3} juice to make it fresh. "Drink this. It's good for your skin," she says. The first time I tried it, I almost spit it out. It tasted like grass! But Mom didn't {4} up. She added more {5}, like apples and pineapples, and used less celery. Now the drink tastes much better. I drink a cup every morning before school. My skin looks better, and I don't get sick as often. Last week, my dad finally tried it. He made a face and said, "It tastes like a salad in a cup." Mom laughed. "That's the point!"

blanks.why: spinach, celery, and other green vegetables「菠菜、芹菜和其他綠色蔬菜」。tickets（票）、villages（村莊）、letters（信）都不能放進果汁機。
加一根香蕉 banana 讓它變甜。ticket（票）、village（村莊）、pocket（口袋）都不能讓飲料變甜。
加一些檸檬 lemon 汁讓它清爽。corner（角落）、uniform（制服）、museum（博物館）都不能做成汁。
give up「放棄」，媽媽沒有放棄，繼續改良。spell（拼字）、marry（結婚）、pray（禱告）都不能和 up 搭配表示放棄。
加更多水果 fruit，例如蘋果和鳳梨。homework（功課）、traffic（交通）、weather（天氣）都不能加進飲料。

passages.zh: 每天早上，我媽媽都會用果汁機打一大杯綠色飲料。她放進菠菜、芹菜和其他綠色蔬菜，再加一根香蕉讓它變甜，加一些檸檬汁讓它更清爽。「喝下去，對皮膚很好。」她說。我第一次喝的時候差點吐出來，喝起來像草一樣！但媽媽沒有放棄，她加了更多水果，像是蘋果和鳳梨，芹菜也放少一點。現在這杯飲料好喝多了。我每天上學前都喝一杯，皮膚變好了，也比較不常生病。上週，爸爸終於也喝了一口。他皺著臉說：「喝起來像一杯沙拉。」媽媽笑著說：「重點就是這個啊！」
